scope: Broaden current peer research across DWG writer maturity, parser/writer security regression classes, Unicode text transport, and binary-DXF projection/carrier routes; reconcile the bounded local FIELD candidate-graph progress without promoting support.

method.kind: Primary peer project README, release notes, generated man page, milestone, stable GDAL DXF driver documentation, and read-only local plan/source inspection
method.researchBoundary: Mutable project documentation and NEWS establish project-reported route limits and fixes only. No external peer output was generated or independently read. The local FIELD graph implementation/build/test is documented separately in the plan and is not peer evidence.

evidence.topic: LibreDWG DWG writer route and version identity
evidence.observed: LibreDWG 0.14.1 beta NEWS reports R2004/AC1018 write support and says R2007 output falls back to R2010/AC1024 because direct R2007 encoding is unsupported. The project README limits reliable writer claims to earlier releases; generated dwgwrite.1 says only R2000 for now; the online Texinfo manual says all formats except R2007 but notes R2010-R2018 still fail CRC and audit checks. These published source surfaces disagree and are mutable.
doesNotEstablish: that a specific peer binary can encode every advertised target
that successful self-read or exit status means an independent CAD reader accepts the file
that R2010-R2018 output passes CRC/audit checks or has correct graph semantics and target magic
any libdxfrw writer defect or support parity
evidence.planUse: Use no peer writer as an oracle from its matrix alone. At one composed run pin the exact source SHA/build profile, record requested and actual six-byte DWG version, hashes, diagnostics/repairs, and independent acceptance. Treat R2007 fallback output as AC1024 when verified.

evidence.topic: LibreDWG safety and progress failure classes
evidence.observed: The 0.14.1 notes include peer fixes for decompressed logical-size versus allocation-capacity divergence; unvalidated R2004 section-page-map offsets; overflowing section-count times decompressed-size arithmetic; R2007 page-offset subtraction underflow; ACIS block-size arithmetic overflow; non-finite angle loops; stale object pointers across reallocating insertion; signed counts bypassing bounds; and pre-R13 no-progress/OOM behavior.
doesNotEstablish: that libdxfrw contains the same bugs
that peer fixes should be copied without matching ODA-backed local evidence
that a full fuzz or sanitizer run is required after every code slice
evidence.planUse: Map only touched analogous code to existing checked-arithmetic, allocation-capacity, offset/progress, finite-number, pointer-lifetime and transaction owners. Add the smallest generated focused negative test per modified path; keep broad fuzz/sanitizer/full suites at composed or scheduled gates.

evidence.topic: GDAL binary-DXF, raw-code, and 3D carrier boundaries
evidence.observed: GDAL 3.12 documents binary-DXF reading and direct binary-to-ASCII translation. Optional RawCodeValues report group codes not handled by the OGR reader, not a complete ordered file archive. AC1027+ extensible mode exposes raw ASM bytes and a transform but does not construct solid geometry.
doesNotEstablish: DWG parsing or DWG writer behavior
full ordered DXF tag preservation or CAD document graph round-trip
ACIS decoding, B-rep validity, or solid geometry correctness
that a binary-to-ASCII direct conversion is an independent semantic writer oracle
evidence.planUse: Keep GDAL optional and composed-only for a specific binary-DXF syntax or unhandled-code question. Record version/options and separate direct conversion, OGR projection, raw unhandled values, and ASM carrier exposure. Do not treat it as a required per-slice test or 3D semantic gate.

evidence.topic: Peer Unicode source-version versus output-version behavior
evidence.observed: Open LibreDWG issue #1414 reports different \U+XXXX treatment in its pre-R2007 TV and R2007+ TU conversion paths when exporting to the same modern DXF target, and flags lone-surrogate escapes as invalid UTF-8. Its author reports a 43-drawing patch comparison, but neither the report nor patch was reproduced in this task.
doesNotEstablish: the intended normative escaping behavior for all DXF string contexts
that libdxfrw has the same version-path defect
that text equivalence implies byte-level or strict-UTF8 equivalence
native consumer acceptance of malformed surrogate output
evidence.planUse: Refine existing text-transport tests with paired runtime-generated/unit-level controls for source TV and TU paths targeting the same modern DXF, assert emitted bytes separately from decoded text, and reject lone-surrogate output under strict UTF-8. Use only a locally authored DWG integration control if needed at a composed gate; do not download or commit a fixture. Keep peer patch measurements advisory and do not create a new finding without local evidence.

evidence.observed: The bounded graph precheck now covers TABLE and non-TABLE extension-dictionary roots, global FIELDLIST membership, owner-matching child links, and object/CadValue references whose target handles exist in the adapter's candidate inventory. Strict targets and the focused named-object callback CTest pass.
doesNotEstablish: that every candidate handle is emitted and remapped exactly once
FIELD root wire semantics, FIELD serialization, or post-write closure
support parity or a native CAD acceptance result
evidence.planUse: Keep FIELD/FIELDLIST export refusal. Next establish producer-origin graph evidence, enumerate actual emitted target handles, verify one-time remapping and readback closure, and resolve the Autodesk/ODA root-code conflict before serializer work.

nextActions: Pin the exact comparator revision and build profile at the existing composed checkpoint; record requested and actual output version.
Tie any local safety test to a changed arithmetic, bounds, progress, pointer-lifetime, or transaction path; do not add routine full-suite runs.
Run GDAL only if a concrete binary-DXF syntax/unhandled-tag question remains; do not use its projection as document or solid semantics.
Use the LibreDWG Unicode issue only to sharpen the existing TV/TU same-target transport test; do not promote the report or patch as a normative rule.
Continue FIELD graph work through producer evidence and actual writer output/remapping closure while keeping serialization fail-closed.
